dorlor_ab.sbatch.header:
dorlor_ab.sbatch — Kim direct 2026-08-21: "DoRA vs LoRA, goa big set, batch 8 GA 2 (or 16
 direct if VRAM suffices), t256, bf16, lr 1e-4, AdamW and Fusion, warmup 1/4 epoch, LR to
 cosine at a knee ~ep8, Fusion with ALL damping fixes, rank 128, 4 nodes x 8 GPUs, 32 epochs.
 I'm mystified why we are getting so bad results now again."

 THE DIAGNOSTIC A/B^2: adapter (DoRA-rows vs plain LoRA) x optimizer (AdamW-WSD vs braked
 Fusion), everything else pinned at the healthiest known settings: TRUE 8-way DDP (torchrun),
 bf16 (=> FA2 on multitorch), T256, per-rank batch 16 default (W's monotonic batch finding;
 BS=8 GA=2 fallback knob), rank 128 alpha 45 (ratified winning value; ALPHA=128 to replicate
 the healthy bf16cmp twins instead), 32 epochs, ckpt every 2.
   - AdamW arms: --lr_schedule wsd (warmup 0.25 ep -> flat -> cosine from ep8) — the FIRST
     scheduled-AdamW runs in the campaign (every prior AdamW run was constant-LR: A2 walk).
   - Fusion arms: --fusion-decay wsd (flat until 25% = ep8, then decay) + --fusion-snr row —
     the full damping kit from the A-series.
 CORPUS CAVEAT recorded up front: bigset is 27.7% near-lossless vs old goa 75.9% (W audit) —
 if all four arms land mediocre-but-healthy, suspect the corpus before the optimizers.

 RUN (4 jobs):
   ARM=dora_adamw  sbatch lumi/sbatch/dorlor_ab.sbatch
   ARM=dora_fusion sbatch lumi/sbatch/dorlor_ab.sbatch
   ARM=lora_adamw  sbatch lumi/sbatch/dorlor_ab.sbatch
   ARM=lora_fusion sbatch lumi/sbatch/dorlor_ab.sbatch
 VERIFY (per job, within minutes): LOCAL_RANK 0..7 once each; steps/epoch ~ 12524/(16*8)=97
   (or /(8*2*8)=97 with the fallback knobs — same optimizer-step count); ckpts UN-versioned;
   AdamW arms print "[lr] WSD: ..." and Fusion arms "[fusion] decay: wsd ...".

aug8_train.sbatch.header:
aug8_train.sbatch — DRAFT (2026-07-23, unsubmitted, for Kim's review): stage 2 of
 the aug8 campaign (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-23-aug8-15ep-campaign.md; renamed
 from aug10 -> aug8 per Kim's ruling — variant set now matches
 mir/src/tools/augment_tracks.py exactly, 8 not 10 variants/crop).
 One standard-g node, 8 GCDs, 8 independent single-GCD arms driven by SLURM_PROCID
 (the ONE-ARM-PER-GCD lane — see the sibling aug8_train_ddp.sbatch for the
 EXPERIMENTAL 8-way-DDP-per-arm alternative Kim asked to try for the walltime risk).
 Skeleton = efp_fp32_compare.sbatch (proven multi-arm one-task-per-GCD pattern);
 fullft flag/behavior = efp_fullft_short.sbatch / efp_fullft_t4096.sbatch. Read those
 three for the deployment rationale this file doesn't re-explain.

 DESIGN (Kim's 2026-07-23 listening verdicts, docs/training-findings.md): fp32 +
 full-finetune sound better than bf16 / adapter-only; rank helps; augmentation SEEMS
 to help; 15 EPOCHS is the new default target (models "start to sound fine after ep5,
 often ep7 is first really good" — prior 8-ep runs were stopping at the threshold of
 good). This campaign crosses the aug8 augmented GOA corpus (+ the EXISTING avp aug
 set, see DATASET PATHS — RESOLVED below) against the two axes Kim's verdict just
 settled (precision, full-ft-vs-adapter), all at 15 epochs, so the next listening pass
 can read off aug's effect ALONGSIDE the precision/rank effect rather than re-deriving
 it separately. GOA-aug8 x AVP(existing aug) x {DoRA-r128, fullft} x {fp32, bf16} =
 8 arms, all --frames 512 (T=512, Kim's T-frames convention, MASTER.md §5) with
 --beat-aware-crop.

 Arms:
   PROCID 0: goa-aug8  DoRA-r128  fp32  T=512  BS=8            lr=1e-4
   PROCID 1: goa-aug8  DoRA-r128  bf16  T=512  BS=8            lr=1e-4
   PROCID 2: goa-aug8  fullft     fp32  T=512  BS=probe(4->1)  lr=1e-4
   PROCID 3: goa-aug8  fullft     bf16  T=512  BS=4            lr=1e-4
   PROCID 4: avp       DoRA-r128  fp32  T=512  BS=8            lr=1e-4
   PROCID 5: avp       DoRA-r128  bf16  T=512  BS=8            lr=1e-4
   PROCID 6: avp       fullft     fp32  T=512  BS=probe(4->1)  lr=1e-4
   PROCID 7: avp       fullft     bf16  T=512  BS=4            lr=1e-4

 LR / RANK / ALPHA convention (grepped from efp_fp32_compare.sbatch, efp_bf16_twin.sbatch,
 efp_fullft_short/t4096.sbatch — all four agree): lr **1e-4** for every arm (DoRA and
 fullft alike; no family here trains at 5e-5); DoRA = `--adapter_type dora-rows --rank
 128 --lora_alpha 128` (alpha=rank, s=1, MASTER §5 convention); fullft = `--full-finetune`
 (unfreezes the whole 1.4B DiT, injects NO adapter, mutually exclusive with the rank/
 adapter flags). `--optimizer fusion` throughout (established default across all four
 reference sbatches).

 BATCH SIZE: DoRA-r128 T=512 BS=8 is PROVEN (efp_fp32_compare arms 4/5, efp_bf16_twin
 arms 0/1 — same T, same rank, both precisions, no probe needed). fullft bf16 T=512
 BS=4 is PROVEN (efp_fullft_short.sbatch arm 2/3: "batch 4 fits T=256/512/1024/2048
 with headroom", no probe). fullft **fp32** T=512 has NO direct precedent (fp32
 fullft was only ever run at T=4096 BS=2 ga=2, a different context length) — fp32
 roughly doubles the full-model param+grad+optimizer-state footprint vs bf16, so
 arms 2/6 get the proven 30-step batch PROBE (efp_fp32_compare's 4->3->2->1 ladder,
 extended down to 1 since a whole-DiT fp32 optimizer state is heavier than a DoRA
 adapter's) rather than assuming BS=4 blindly.

 EPOCH-TIME ESTIMATE — ASSUMPTION, NOT MEASURED (10-min grep of WORKLOG/journals
 found no per-epoch T=512/aug8 timing; the one hard number available is
 docs/training-findings.md's "~2.4 s/step" for SA3 DoRA at T~512 BS1, and
 efp_fp32_compare's own note that its T=4096 BS1 goa arm — 5400 steps/epoch, ~2-4
 s/step — "may hit the 48h wall around epoch 5-8"). Reasoning chain: GOA-aug8 is
 ~5400 orig + up to 5400x8=43200 aug crops (BPM-cap dedup likely trims the average
 below 8/crop slightly) ≈ **~43-48k crops**. At BS=8, T=512 (8x shorter context than
 the T=4096 arm above, so materially cheaper per step despite ~8x more crops and 8x
 the batch — steps/epoch ≈ 45000/8 ≈ 5600, roughly the SAME step COUNT as the
 T=4096/BS1 arm's 5400, but each step should be substantially cheaper at T=512):
 **DoRA arms: order ~1-2h/epoch -> 15-30h for 15 epochs (fits the 47h wall).**
 fullft arms do more work per step (whole-DiT backward + bigger optimizer) at a
 SMALLER batch (4 or probed-down), i.e. MORE steps/epoch than DoRA -> **fullft bf16:
 order ~2-4h/epoch -> 30-60h; fullft fp32 (smallest probed batch): likely the
 arm(s) that DON'T finish 15 epochs in one 47h job.** Per-epoch checkpoints (below)
 make partial completion useful regardless — re-submit with --resume_ckpt to
 continue past a wall-clock cutoff, OR see aug8_train_ddp.sbatch (Kim's requested
 DDP experiment: same 8 GCDs applied to ONE arm at a time instead of 8 arms in
 parallel, ~8x less wall-clock per arm). AVP arms (2393 base crops, ~10-20x smaller
 than GOA-aug8's) will finish 15 epochs comfortably early and idle their GCD —
 acceptable, matches the fp32cmp/fullft campaigns' own convention.

 DATASET PATHS — RESOLVED (Kim's ruling, 2026-07-23):
   GOA-aug8 = original goa crops + the aug8 output from aug8_encode.sbatch, as TWO
   comma-separated --encoded_dir sources (train_lora.py supports multi-source
   --encoded_dir/--caption_sidecar natively):
     ${FLASH}/latents_sa3,${FLASH}/latents_goa_aug8
   AVP: reuse the EXISTING latents_avp aug set AS-IS — no new avp augmentation is
   generated for this campaign. (This also makes the earlier open question — the
   `latents_avp_aug10` naming collision with the 320-crop small-set control from
   docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-winning-fp32-run-plan.md — MOOT: nothing here
   writes to or reads that path.)

 CAPTIONS: inherited default (longform sidecars, PROBS=0,0,1) — same override knobs
 as efp_fp32_compare.sbatch (CAPTIONS=stored, SIDECAR=, PROBS=). Augmented crops carry
 their PARENT crop's inherited prompt (see encode_aug_task.py) so the sidecar's
 per-source-track lookup still resolves for them.

 CAVEAT — beat-aware crop on augmented latents: --beat-aware-crop falls back to
 uniform-random sub-cropping for any latent lacking a sibling .TIMESERIES.npz
 (dataset.py, confirmed) — the aug8 latents from encode_aug_task.py do NOT carry
 one (not built in this draft). So the original 5400 goa crops (and existing avp
 crops) get true beat-aligned T=512 sub-crops; the aug8 variants get uniform-random
 ones. Flagged as an open question in the campaign spec, not fixed here.

 PREREQS: code+SIF+models pre-staged; latents_sa3.tar.gz + latents_avp.tar.gz (existing)
 AND latents_goa_aug8.tar.gz (aug8_encode.sbatch output) on ${SCRATCH}; code tarball
 refreshed from the WORKING TREE (never `git archive` — lumi-ops rule) so
 scripts/train_lora.py carries --full-finetune and --frames.

ftstack_heads.sbatch.header:
ftstack_heads.sbatch — B9: the control stack retrained ON TOP of our best FULL FINETUNE
 (CONTINUITY 2026-08-21, Kim direct: "take our best full finetune, and train our FiLM,
 melody and LATCH heads with best known values and Fusion on top of that instead of the
 base model").

 8 single-GCD arms on one node:
   r0  Head-B FiLM (melody_contour) on the FULL-FT backbone   <- the backbone-dependent piece
   r1  Head-B FiLM on medium-base                             <- matched control (same seed)
   r2  f0_other melody head   r3  f0_bass melody head         <- D3 best values (EMA 0.999,
   r4  hpcp                   r5  rms_energy_bass                 val split BY SOURCE TRACK)
   r6  onset_envelope         r7  spectral_flatness           <- strongest steering features
 Heads (r2-7) are latent readouts (backbone-free by construction) — retrained here with the
 BEST KNOWN recipe: Fusion SF-NorMuon (ns5,normuon,sf) + adaln_zero + bf16 hot dtype + EMA
 0.999 + cosine fusion-decay (the braked Fusion — undamped NS5 is the drone mechanism) +
 held-out val split by source_track (83329a8: crop-split leaks sibling crops).

 KNOB (required): FT_CKPT=/scratch/.../runs/fullft_fleet/<arm>/epoch=N.ckpt  (FAT ckpt; the
   EMA shadow weights are loaded — that is what deploys). Candidates, best-first:
   - today's fullft_fleet arms (AdamW matched controls, EMA on): fullft_avpaug/mix3/suomi/...
   - fullft_mixed_wdfix (completed, bounded-norm, z0 std 1.134 healthy)
   - the precision-ladder fp16 arm (Kim's "sound of its own" pick)

 PREREQ on LUMI: latents_sa3/*.TIMESERIES.npz co-located with latents (rsync ~3.1G — .npz
   does NOT collide with the dataset's *.npy glob); ${SCRATCH}/latents_sa3_melody/ (melody8
   streams, ~10M); code: control/ + stable-audio-3/scripts/latch/ synced.
 RUN:  FT_CKPT=/scratch/.../epoch=N.ckpt sbatch lumi/sbatch/ftstack_heads.sbatch

dora256_mixed_2x4gpu.sbatch.header:
dora256_mixed_2x4gpu.sbatch — CONTINUITY 2026-08-17 (Kim direct, after the full-FT DDP-bug
 saga tonight: "with all the trouble we've having with full finetunes, let's also run... rank
 256 DoRA, FP32, alpha 196" then corrected "why single GPU? Run on four. And another four with
 5e-5 but alpha 128" then "EMA and warmup on, and Adagc"). Two DoRA arms on ONE 8-GPU node,
 4 real DDP-synced GPUs each, same mixed avp+goa T4096 dataset as
 fullft_mixed_avp_goa_t4096.sbatch:
   arm A (GPUs 0-3): rank=256 alpha=196 lr=1e-4
   arm B (GPUs 4-7): rank=256 alpha=128 lr=5e-5

 ✅ STATUS: VERIFIED WORKING. Smoke job 21330059 (2026-08-17) formed BOTH 4-way DDP groups:
 `grep -h LOCAL_RANK <log> | sort | uniq -c` gave LOCAL_RANK 0,1,2,3 each exactly TWICE, with
 CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES [0,1,2,3] per group (arm B's ROCR set 4-7 correctly renumbers to logical
 0-3), both srun steps COMPLETED 0:0, arms concurrent (each step 4m34s inside a 4m36s job).
 Full run: job 21330736. See ROUND 3 below for the launch that achieves this; the two blocks
 immediately following are SUPERSEDED and kept only as a record of the wrong turns.

 ── ROUND 1 (SUPERSEDED, kept for the record) ── the original reasoning was that splitting one
 node into TWO independent 4-GPU DDP groups needs each group to see its OWN scoped
 SLURM_NTASKS=4/SLURM_PROCID=0..3, since Lightning's SLURMEnvironment derives world_size/rank
 from those, so the plan was TWO separate srun job STEPS each with --ntasks=4 --exclusive,
 letting SLURM's step scheduler hand each arm a disjoint GPU set. That is NOT what the script
 does now: the SLURMEnvironment premise is exactly the thing that turned out to be unreliable
 (see ROUND 3), so per-arm scoping now comes from torchrun, GPU disjointness from an explicit
 ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES, and the steps use --overlap rather than --exclusive. What DID survive
 from this round: backgrounding each arm with `&` plus a trailing `wait`, so the two arms run
 concurrently rather than sequentially.

 EMA (Kim asked for it explicitly): train_lora.py FORCE-DISABLES EMA for DoRA/LoRA adapters
 regardless of the flag (full-finetune only) -- passing --use-ema here is a harmless no-op,
 not withheld, just doesn't do anything for this adapter type. Flagging so it isn't mistaken
 for silently working.

 ── ROUND 3, THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY WORKS (2026-08-17) ── migrated to the CSC/LUMI reference
 torchrun launch, after job 21251551 PROVED it on the sibling full-FT script: real DDP
 confirmed by LOCAL_RANK 0..7 (not eight 0s), ZERO -vN duplicate checkpoints, and
 244 steps/epoch vs the broken run's 1948 (= 1948/8, i.e. genuine 8-way data sharding), in
 3h41m instead of 1d8h. Per arm here: ONE srun --overlap task, explicit ROCR_VISIBLE_DEVICES
 (0-3 / 4-7), and `torchrun --nproc-per-node=4` with a PER-ARM rdzv port (two rendezvous
 servers on one node collide on a shared port). Requires train_lora.py's
 torch.cuda.set_device(LOCAL_RANK) fix (guarded in the preflight below).

 ── ROUND 2 (SUPERSEDED AND HALF-WRONG -- read the warning) ── this block recorded removing
 --devices 4 per arm, which HAD crashed both arms outright (job 21245642.1,
 MisconfigurationException: "You requested gpu: [0,1,2,3] But your machine only has: [0]" --
 under cgroup isolation each process only ever sees ONE device, so --devices N>1 always fails).
 That crash diagnosis is CORRECT and still holds: do not add --devices back.
 ⚠️ BUT the conclusion drawn from it was WRONG, and it is the precise false belief that cost two
 node allocations, so it is spelled out rather than deleted: this block claimed
 fullft_avp_aug.sbatch (job #68) was "the actual proven precedent" showing --gpus-per-task=1 with
 no --devices lets Lightning's SLURMEnvironment form the DDP group from SLURM_NTASKS alone.
 IT DOES NOT. That pattern SILENTLY fails to form a group -- every rank logs LOCAL_RANK: 0 and
 you get N uncoordinated single-GPU trainers writing colliding -vN checkpoints, no crash and no
 hang. #68's in-file comment was evidence about one job, not a guarantee; it was never verified
 with the LOCAL_RANK check. Removing --devices was necessary but not sufficient -- ROUND 3 (the
 torchrun launch) is what actually forms the group.

 RUN: SMOKE=1 sbatch lumi/sbatch/dora256_mixed_2x4gpu.sbatch   (bounded ~20 steps/arm, verify
      BOTH arms print world_size=4 with 4 distinct local GPUs, no crash/hang, ckpts appear)
      — PASSED 2026-08-17 as job 21330059, see STATUS at the top of this header.
      then: sbatch lumi/sbatch/dora256_mixed_2x4gpu.sbatch      (full, open only after SMOKE passes)

subloss_tgate_modes.sbatch.header:
subloss_tgate_modes.sbatch — R2(t)-GATE MODE A/B + seed pairs (burn-day, Kim 2026-08-21)
 (CONTINUITY 2026-08-06). Identical to subspace_loss_grid_mt.sbatch EXCEPT the subspace basis:
 melody_subspace15_selective_v3.npz instead of _v2. This is the A/B that Kim's melody
 machinery-audit motivated. The v2 basis (top-15 melody VARIANCE) had ~ZERO melody-vs-codec-noise
 selectivity on held-out data (SNR 1.0x) — so upweighting it boosts codec hiss as much as melody,
 the probable reason #59 came back weak. v3 (whitened CSP: signal=atlas interval deltas, noise=
 real codec deltas+timbre) is 5.1x melody-over-codec-noise on held-out. See
 eval/musicology/melody_selective_subspace_2026-08-06/VERDICT.md.

 ARMS (single-GCD, small-g): K in {2, 5, 12} — matched to the v2 grid so v3 arms compare
 directly against the already-run subloss_goa_k{2,5,12} (v2) + the shared lreq_goa_lr1e4 (K=1)
 baseline. RECIPE = lreq_goa_lr1e4 EXACTLY (nothing but the basis differs from the v2 grid).
 Diffs vs sa3.sif version: MTSIF + sa3_train_venv_mt overlay, PYTHONPATH append+first, no

morph_head_sweep.sbatch.header:
morph_head_sweep.sbatch — 8-arm melody control-head sweep, one 8-GCD node. CONTINUITY 2026-08-12 (Kim-greenlit).

 THIS IS SWEEP-1 = the CONFIG-READY arms only: it varies the FIRST-ORDER levers we can drive with existing
 flags — INJECTION SITE (--adapter-layers, Head-A's pivot), OPTIMIZER (Fusion vs AdamW; Fusion was sovereign
 for onset density), CAPACITY (dora-rank), TARGET among existing modes (melody_contour vs hpcp-attribute),
 and CFG/melody DROPOUT (Zach's overfit knob). Base recipe = the proven headb_melody.sbatch, moved onto
 FusionOpt. The MORPHOLOGICAL arms (soft-rank/contour loss, k=3 temporal kernel, per-window rank-norm target,
 chroma384 attribute) need CODE + DATA that don't exist yet -> SWEEP-2, after C implements the flags.

 aug8_encode/muscriptor pattern). Today's saga: --gpus-per-task=1 put all 8 arms on GCD0 -> OOM/collision.
 ENV: sa3.sif — the KNOWN-GOOD control-head env (headb note: local ROCm-7.15 pilot heap-corrupted; sa3.sif green).

 RUN ORDER (today's hard lesson — always smoke an 8-GCD node job first):
   SMOKE=1 sbatch morph_head_sweep.sbatch     # ~10 min; confirm [gpu-assign] shows ROCR 0..7 DISTINCT, no crash
   sbatch        morph_head_sweep.sbatch       # full 15-epoch run

mirctrl_bracket.sbatch.header:
mirctrl_bracket.sbatch — B7 MIR-timeseries conditioner bracket (CONTINUITY 2026-08-21,
 Kim direct: "train some really traditional models, using our mir data as conditioners,
 probably rank 32 DoRAs ... target is every feature we have ... goa+avp aug mixed set").

 WHAT EACH ARM IS: medium-base + DoRA-rows rank 32 + a zero-init per-frame additive
 control projection (the DiT's native modular local-cond inlet, installed on blocks
 12-23 = W's layer-map union) fed with REAL MIR curves from the target crop
 (teacher-forced; per-item control dropout 0.2 = the CFG null). The PACK knob picks the
 feature family; 'all' = every field we have (36 ch: band-RMS 4, stem RMS/onset 8,
 rhythm 3, HPCP 12, spectral 4, position 1, f0 4 [goa-only, zero-filled on avp]).

 SELF-REPORTING (train-now-evaluate-later, allocation ends imminently): every arm
 (a) measures the CONTROL-ABLATION meter in-training every 500 steps — RF loss on a
     fixed batch under {true, shuffled, zero} control; control_gain > 0 <=> the model
     exploits the time-ALIGNED control (B7 kill-criterion readable from the log alone);
 (b) writes report.md + report.json + control_ablation.jsonl into the run dir at fit
     end, with an sbatch-epilogue fallback for walltime-truncated runs.

 DATASET (fixed): latents_sa3 (goa 5400) + latents_avp (avp aug 2393) with their
 PROVEN longform sidecars (the winning fp32 family pairing). NOT biggoa (Kim: issues).
 PREREQ on ${SCRATCH}: latents_sa3/, latents_avp/, latents_sa3_ctrl/, latents_avp_ctrl/
   (the _ctrl dirs come from build_ctrl_packs.py locally + rsync; they are SIBLINGS on
   purpose — a .ctrl.npy INSIDE a latent dir gets globbed as a latent by the dataset).

 BRACKET (one arm per job; priority order if budget is short):
   PACK=all      sbatch lumi/sbatch/mirctrl_bracket.sbatch     # 1. the headline arm
   PACK=melody   sbatch ...                                    # 2. the melody-wall arm
   PACK=rhythm   sbatch ...                                    # 3. the channel SA3 keeps
   PACK=dynamics sbatch ...                                    # 4.
   PACK=stems    sbatch ...                                    # 5.
   PACK=spectral sbatch ...                                    # 6.
   PACK=all BLOCKS=all sbatch ...                              # 7. blocks ablation
   PACK=all RANK=64    sbatch ...                              # 8. capacity ablation

lr5e5_allsets.sbatch.header:
lr5e5_allsets.sbatch — Kim direct 2026-08-22, after auditioning
 renders/length_variant/adamw_goa_t512_bs4_lr5e5__ep9__cfg16__w100__*: "the 5e-5 clips sound
 better than 1e-4, 2e-4 shows degradation, and where 1e-4/2e-4 MELT at cfg16/w2 the 5e-5 can
 take that push and still sound musical — which speaks to some deeper very healthy structure."
 => REPLICATE THAT RUN'S RECIPE IN FULL, across every sound set we have, to ep48.

 THE RUN BEING REPLICATED: runs/adamw_bf16_sweep/adamw_goa_t512_bs4_lr5e5 (arm 7 of
 efp_adamw_bf16_sweep.sbatch, 2026-07-24). Its ACTUAL settings, read off run_meta + sbatch:
   dora-rows r128 ALPHA 128 (not 45), AdamW wd0.01 betas[0.9,0.95], lr 5e-5 CONSTANT (no
   schedule), bf16, T=512 beat-aware, goa longform sidecar at caption tiers 0,0,1 (t3 ONLY),
   NO warmup flag, seed 1 -- and batch 4 on ONE GCD, i.e. EFFECTIVE BATCH 4. That sweep ran
   8 independent single-GCD arms off SLURM_PROCID; it was never DDP.
 TWO DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS, both forced, both recorded so nobody reads this as a pure replicate:
   1. EFFECTIVE BATCH 8, not 4. Single-GCD at eff-4 puts a ~21.6k-crop mix at ~110 min/epoch =
      88 h to ep48, which does not fit the allocation. 8-way DDP at BS=1 is the closest
      reachable regime (eff 8 = 2x, vs eff 32 if we kept BS=4 across 8 ranks = 8x and a
      different experiment). lr stays 5e-5 -- the variable Kim isolated.
   2. MIXED CORPUS, not goa alone (that is the point of the run).
 NOT A DEVIATION, deliberately kept: alpha 128, constant lr, T512, beat-aware, t3-only goa
 captions. The dorlor lane uses alpha 45 / WSD / T256 / 0.6,0.3,0.1 -- copying it here would
 have changed four things at once and thrown away what Kim actually heard.

 CORPUS MIX (--encoded_dir order; per-source sidecars + per-source caption tiers):
   goa     latents_sa3          5400   w 1.00   goa_longform_sidecar          0,0,1
   bigset  latents_goa_bigset  12524   w 0.18   goa_bigset_hinted_bylatent    0,0,1
   avpaug  latents_avp          ~2400  w 1.00   avp_captions_tiered           0,0.9,0.1
   suomi   suomisoundi_latents   1261   w 1.00   suomisoundi_caption_sidecar   0.25,0.45,0.30
 BIGSET WEIGHT: Kim asked for "maybe 20% chance because it's got mp3 sources more than the
 others". Natural proportion would be 58%; w=0.18 lands it at ~20% of draws. It also rides
 tiers 0,0,1 because its granite tier measured NOT GROUNDED (folder-name derived, rare-term
 recall 1.24x vs chance) -- per-source probs exist precisely so that cannot poison the mix.

 AUG=1: appends latents_goa_aug8 (3941 bungee-augmented goa crops) as a 5th source, sharing
 the goa sidecar -- the same clean+aug pairing aug8_train_ddp.sbatch used. NOTE: train_lora's
 --augment is live-encode ONLY ("No effect on --encoded_dir"), so there is no on-the-fly
 augmentation available on the pre-encoded latent path. Pre-augmented dirs are the only route.

   MODE=hyperball LR=3e-5 | MODE=hyperball LR=1e-4     <- #1
   MODE=edm2      LR=3e-5 | MODE=edm2      LR=1e-4     <- #2

 ALL SIX ARE READY (2026-08-17): --forced-weight-norm landed in stable-audio-3 1d6474c with 12
 tests. What the two bounds actually differ in, since the arms are only worth running if they are
 not the same experiment:
   hyperball -> whole-tensor ‖W‖_F FROZEN at ‖W0‖_F, optimizer-side, on EVERY spectral matrix.
                Output magnitude cannot change at all.
   edm2      -> per-output-channel DIRECTION normalised with a LEARNABLE per-channel gain, on the
                output projection only (transformer.py:1171). Magnitude can still adapt, but
                through one well-conditioned parameter per channel instead of drifting across the
                whole matrix. Strictly the weaker, more expressive constraint.
   both      -> hyperball on the bulk + per-channel gain control at the output.
 Both are retrofit-safe (each reproduces the pretrained function at step 0, so no fine-tune spike).

 WHY THESE TWO BOUNDS AND NOT MORE WARMUP/EMA/AdaGC: warmup, EMA and AdaGC all shape the PATH,
 none bounds the DESTINATION. Warmup only delays onset (equilibrium norm unchanged); EMA averages a
 drifting trajectory so the average drifts too; AdaGC clips against an EMA of recent clipped norms,
 so it catches SPIKES while sustained drift passes every test unremarked. Hyperball and EDM2-style
 forced weight norm are the two retrofit-safe options that put a HARD bound on ‖W‖. Full reasoning +
 the 12-paper read: papers/CONTINUITY-drone-optimizer-synthesis-2026-08-11.md.

fullft_avp_subloss.sbatch.header:
fullft_avp_subloss.sbatch — Kim direct 2026-08-22 (~03:00), "let one run roll on alone":
 AVP, T1024, lr 2.5e-5, FULL-FT, AdamW (wd at default), subspace-loss weighting in, schedule
 flat until ep10 then cosine, to ep64. "This one has a very mellow LR and some nice controls
 that have been helpful."

 THREE THINGS RESOLVED BEFORE WRITING THIS, all of which changed the spec:
  1. ADAGC IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. No flag, no code, anywhere in the trainer or optimizer. It exists
     for us only as EXPERIMENTS E2, a PLANNED bracket on the LatCH melody head. Dropped -- it
     would have to be written, not enabled.
  2. SPECTRAL WD IS FUSIONOPT-ONLY (build_fusion_param_groups -> per-group weight_decay on the 2D
     DiT matrices). Under --optimizer adamw there is no such path; --weight_decay is plain
     decoupled AdamW decay. Kim: "AdamW WD can be at default" => omitted entirely (0.01).
  3. LIVE ENCODE CANNOT DELIVER THE AUGMENTATION KIM WANTS. --augment (live-encode only) covers
     sub_frame_shift / gain / stereo_width / polarity. PITCH SHIFT AND TIME STRETCH ARE
     --aug-heavy ONLY, and that path lazily loads torchaudio transforms -- the sox-adjacent thing
     CLAUDE.md bans in favour of bungee. Kim: "bungee augs will be mandatory, especially the
     pitch augs". Bungee is OFFLINE (CPU, HyperQueue) by construction, so the ONLY route to
     bungee pitch augmentation is a PRE-AUGMENTED, PRE-ENCODED latent dir. Hence this trains on
     latents_avp (the existing avp aug set, 2394 crops) and NOT on a --data_dir live-encode.
     Kim's own instinct -- "SAMEs encode fast on CPU, could we pre-calculate in parallel?" -- is
     exactly right and is already built: aug8_encode.sbatch is a two-phase CPU-bungee-then-
     SAME-L-encode job on one node. It is not a tonight job (its bungee_python-in-container risk
     is still open, and $SCRATCH/avp_src showed no wav/flac at depth<=3).

 SUBSPACE WEIGHT — Kim 2026-08-22 asked for "something which we know to work... the latest".
 THERE IS NO EARS-RATIFIED K. Weights tried: 2/5/12 (the v3sel grid, trained to ep19), 20 (goa),
 24 (the most recent lane, 4 corpora). EXPERIMENTS B1: the quartet's renders only landed after
 F caught that the tgate arm had never been rendered despite being reported as such, and the
 whole set still awaits Kim's ears. So K=12 is chosen as the top of the COMPLETED grid and the
 value the k24 lane itself names as its baseline -- not as a winner, because none is known.
 NOT K=24: that lane ran DoRA at eff batch 64 / lr 8e-5; this is full-FT at eff 8 / lr 2.5e-5,
 and a 5x-the-grid-midpoint weight transferred across that gap could dominate the loss.
 Basis is v3sel (melody-SELECTIVE, whitened CSP, 2026-08-06) = the FIXED lever; v2 is older.
 NO TGATE here on purpose: the deficit-vs-r2 mode A/B is running RIGHT NOW (21439464), and
 adding tgate would preempt the result that decides how to set it.
 EXPECTATION-SETTING, recorded so this run is not oversold: our own reading is that the melody
 wall is structural (melody is relational; no linear channel subspace captures it) and subspace
 loss is a "+10-15% tool", not the wall-breaker. The conditioning lane (B9/D12) is that.

 CAPTIONS: avp_captions_tiered.json, tiers 0,0.9,0.1 -- AVP granite measured 3.84x rare-term

fullft_reg_ab.sbatch.header:
fullft_reg_ab.sbatch — REGULARIZATION A/B for the full-FT latent-scale runaway (CONTINUITY 2026-08-10).
 Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-fullft-regularization-ab.md

 WHY: the first A/B (fullft_wd_ab.sbatch) showed plain weight_decay 0.1 BOUNDS the FusionOpt full-FT
 latent-scale runaway (global std 0.7->5.6 ep3->ep7; #chan>2.0 0->166/256). But wd is BLUNT — it shrinks
 every weight direction, incl. the subtle feature-bearing ones we're trying to strengthen. This job tests
 whether GENTLER / MORE TARGETED regularizers bound the runaway with less collateral on fine detail:
   - AGC (Adaptive Gradient Clipping, NFNets): scale-relative per-output-unit grad clip — reins in only
     large-grad-relative-to-scale units (--grad-clip-mode agc --agc-lambda 0.01).
   - output-std penalty: penalize z0_hat's per-channel std drifting off the data's, in the LOSS not the
     weights, gated to low noise (--output-std-penalty LOUT --output-std-t-gate 0.5). Logs both stds to
     the CSV each step so the runaway is readable WITHOUT a render.

 8 arms = {limiter} x {output-reg} at wd 0.01, + wd/wd-full references (1 arm per GCD, single-GPU each —
 the precision_ladder / fullft_wd_ab pattern, which itself droned, so the reg comparison is faithful).
 Reproduces the failing setup: full-FT, big goa set via LIVE-ENCODE (--data_dir + sidecar, like
 fullft_bigset), bf16-mixed (Kim: speed; a precision confound vs the fp32 #68, but the reg comparison is
 INTERNAL so it holds), T512, bs4, 10ep, FusionOpt(all-on)+EMA. Tail renders the cfg16 canary per
 checkpoint + prints the latent-std table (same probe as wd_ab): anchor should climb (positive control);
 a winner tracks ~1.0 with 0 non-finite AND retains detail >= the `wd` baseline (Kim's ears + DSP proxy).

subspace_loss_grid.sbatch.header:
subspace_loss_grid.sbatch — SUBSPACE-WEIGHTED RF LOSS grid (CONTINUITY 2026-07-30,
 Kim direct). Counter to diffusion spectral bias (tau ~ 1/lambda, arXiv 2503.03206):
 melody = a measured 15-dim latent subspace holding only 9.3% of corpus variance, so
 plain RF gradient-starves it. This grid upweights the RF error's melody-subspace
 component by K (loss = mse + (K-1)*subspace_share; K=1 is byte-identical off).

 ARMS (single-GCD, small-g): K in {2, 5, 12}  (12 ~ 1/variance-share).
 RECIPE = lreq_goa_lr1e4 EXACTLY (goa latents, dora-rows r128 a128, adamw, bf16, T512
 beat-aware, bs4, lr 1e-4, 20 ep, ckpt every 4) => the lr-equiv middle arm IS the K=1
 baseline — no extra baseline burn. Render tail identical (cfg7, w{1,1.5,2,3}).

 READOUT (post-pull): board cells + muscriptor contour-repetition (the hook-decile
 axis) + melody-subspace variance share of generated latents vs baseline.
